portName: Centre Saint-John Perse cruise terminal, Pointe-à-Pitre
seoTitle: Pointe-à-Pitre cruise port guide: town, Mémorial ACTe, Gosier
seoDescription: Ships dock at Centre Saint-John Perse: 10–15 min walk to Place de la Victoire, 15 min more to Mémorial ACTe, 15 min taxi to Datcha beach. Shops shut Sunday.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the Centre Saint-John Perse cruise terminal in the middle of Pointe-à-Pitre, and Place de la Victoire and the markets are a 10–15 minute walk away, so you need no transport for the town. For a beach, take a taxi about 15 minutes to Plage de la Datcha in Le Gosier. Be back at the ship 60 minutes before all-aboard, and leave the town centre 75 minutes before.
intro: Pointe-à-Pitre is Guadeloupe's commercial town, not a resort, and the cruise terminal is part of it. You walk out of Centre Saint-John Perse into a grid of streets with covered markets, an iron-framed cathedral and Place de la Victoire facing the old harbour. The big draw is the Mémorial ACTe, a museum of the slave trade and slavery on the site of the old Darboussier sugar works. Beaches are in Le Gosier and Sainte-Anne along the south coast. Check what day you are in port: on Sundays most shops close and buses barely run.

terminals.name: Centre Saint-John Perse cruise terminal
terminals.notes: In central Pointe-à-Pitre. Two terminal buildings, able to handle three ships at once, with free Wi-Fi, duty-free shops, craft stalls, a tourist information desk and access for passengers with reduced mobility. Taxi stands with posted rates are outside the gates. Ferries to Marie-Galante and Les Saintes leave nearby.

walkability.detail: Place de la Victoire, the Darse waterfront, the markets and the cathedral are a 10–15 minute walk from the terminal on flat town streets. The Mémorial ACTe is about 15 minutes' walk further south of Place de la Victoire. Beaches need a taxi or car.

transportSections.time: 10–15 min to Place de la Victoire
transportSections.detail: Flat streets from the terminal to the town centre. Continue south about 15 minutes to the Mémorial ACTe, or take a short taxi ride in the heat.

transportSections.cost: Fares set by regulation and posted at the stand; confirm the price before you go (2026)
transportSections.time: About 15 min to Plage de la Datcha (Le Gosier); about 30 min to Sainte-Anne
transportSections.detail: Taxi stands are outside the terminal gates. Drivers usually take euros and often US dollars. Expect surcharges at night, at weekends and on public holidays. Arrange the return pick-up before you leave, because taxis are scarcer at the beaches.

transportSections.cost: Check current fare in the Karu'lis app or with the driver
transportSections.detail: The Karu'lis urban network links Pointe-à-Pitre with Le Gosier and Sainte-Anne. Buses run mainly Monday to Friday, with reduced Saturday service and only a few weekend lines on Sundays. Timetables are often not kept, so the bus is a poor choice on a tight port day.

transportSections.cost: About €27–45 a day (2025 prices); deposit usually €800–1,000
transportSections.time: Needed for Deshaies, Saint-François or the Basse-Terre rainforest
transportSections.detail: Driving is on the right. Weekday traffic jams around Pointe-à-Pitre build from 16:00, which is when you will be driving back.

returnTiming.rule: Be back at the ship 60 minutes before all-aboard. Leave the town centre 75 minutes before, the Mémorial ACTe 90 minutes before, Plage de la Datcha 90 minutes before and Sainte-Anne 2 hours 15 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: Weekday traffic around Pointe-à-Pitre builds from about 16:00, just when beach-goers drive back. Taxis are easy at the terminal but harder to find at the beaches, so book the return when you are dropped off. Do not attempt a ferry to Marie-Galante or Les Saintes on a port day unless the crossing times leave a wide margin; ferry schedules can change with the weather.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: From Le Gosier, ask a beach restaurant to call a taxi, or walk to the main road and hail one. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

diyVsExcursion.saving: The whole cost of a town tour

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Taxi about 15 minutes each way; beach free
diyVsExcursion.saving: Depends on taxi fare and group size

excursionAdvice: Do the town and the Mémorial ACTe on your own: both are walkable from the terminal. Le Gosier is an easy taxi ride for a beach afternoon. A ship tour is worth it for anything on Basse-Terre, such as the rainforest, waterfalls or Deshaies, and for Sainte-Anne or Saint-François on a short call, because the drives are 30–60 minutes each way and afternoon traffic can turn a 30-minute run into much longer.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30, on a weekday when shops and markets are open.

steps.what: Walk from the terminal to Place de la Victoire, 10–15 minutes. Pick up a map at the tourist information point.
Marché de la Darse on the waterfront for fruit and fish, then the covered Marché Saint-Antoine for spices.
Cathédrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul, with its riveted iron frame, and the Musée Saint-John Perse in a 19th-century Creole house on rue Nozières.
Walk about 15 minutes south to the Mémorial ACTe. Allow two hours.
Taxi to Plage de la Datcha in Le Gosier, about 15 minutes. Lunch at one of the beach restaurants and agree the taxi pick-up time.
Swim, or take a shuttle boat to Îlet du Gosier.
Taxi back to the terminal, leaving Datcha 90 minutes before all-aboard at the latest (by 16:00).
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Mémorial ACTe
sights.why: A large museum and memorial on the history of the slave trade, slavery and its abolition, built on the site of the old Darboussier sugar works; audioguides are available, including in English.
sights.cost: Ticket required; check memorial-acte.fr for the current price
sights.tip: About 15 minutes' walk south of Place de la Victoire. It has exceptional closures (for example 14–18 February 2026), so check before you go.

sights.name: Place de la Victoire
sights.why: The town's large shaded square of mango trees and royal palms, lined by cafés and old houses and facing the Darse harbour.

sights.name: Marché Saint-Antoine (covered market)
sights.why: The main market for spices, produce and local goods in the town centre.
sights.tip: Go in the morning. Most shops close on Sunday and many on Saturday afternoon.

sights.name: Marché de la Darse
sights.why: Waterfront market on the old harbour with fresh fish, tropical fruit, spices, crafts and flowers.
sights.tip: Combine with Place de la Victoire next door.

sights.name: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul
sights.why: The town's main church, built with arches of riveted iron beams; known locally as the cathedral.
sights.tip: On rue du Général Ruillier, a few minutes from Place de la Victoire.

sights.name: Musée Saint-John Perse
sights.why: Municipal museum in a 19th-century colonial house: a Creole interior on the ground floor and the life and work of the Nobel poet, who grew up in Guadeloupe, upstairs.
sights.tip: At 9 rue de Nozières; phone +590 590 90 01 92 to check hours.

sights.name: Musée Schoelcher
sights.why: Museum dedicated to Victor Schoelcher, who campaigned for the abolition of slavery in the French colonies, with exhibits on the slave trade and works of art.
sights.tip: At 24 rue Peynier; pairs well with the Mémorial ACTe.

sights.name: Plage de la Datcha and Îlet du Gosier
sights.why: The nearest proper beach, in Le Gosier, with restaurants, sunbeds and shuttle boats to the small island offshore with its old lighthouse.
sights.cost: Beach free; sunbeds and boats extra
sights.tip: About 15 minutes by taxi. Book the return pick-up.

beaches.name: Plage de la Datcha (Le Gosier)
beaches.note: Restaurants, snack stands, sunbeds, umbrellas and showers. Shuttle boats to Îlet du Gosier.

beaches.name: Plage de la Caravelle (Sainte-Anne)
beaches.note: Only on a long call; afternoon traffic back into Pointe-à-Pitre can be heavy.

beaches.name: Plage Bois Jolan (Sainte-Anne)
beaches.note: Too far for most port days.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting a lively town on a Sunday.
commonMistakes.fix: Shops close on Sunday and often on Saturday and Wednesday afternoons, and buses barely run. On a Sunday, plan the Mémorial ACTe (if open) and a beach by taxi.
Many shops close from 12:00 to 14:00. Do the markets and shops in the morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on the bus to get back from the beach.
commonMistakes.fix: Karu'lis buses are infrequent and often off-schedule. Use a taxi and book the return pick-up.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking a ferry to Les Saintes or Marie-Galante on a port day.
commonMistakes.fix: Ferry times change with the weather, and missing the boat back means missing the ship. Book the ship's excursion if you want the islands.

commonMistakes.mistake: Driving back from Sainte-Anne or Basse-Terre late in the afternoon.
commonMistakes.fix: Weekday traffic around Pointe-à-Pitre builds from 16:00. Leave Sainte-Anne at least 2 hours 15 minutes before all-aboard.

safety: The terminal and town centre are generally fine to explore on foot in daytime. Keep valuables secure and stay aware in the crowded markets. On Sundays the commercial streets empty out; local authorities have been working on Sunday activity and safety in the town for cruise visitors, but stick to the main squares and waterfront when it is quiet. Seaweed (sargassum) can wash up on some beaches in season, so check conditions before taking a taxi to a beach. Guadeloupe is part of France and EU emergency numbers work.
accessibility: The cruise terminal is equipped for passengers with reduced mobility. The walk to Place de la Victoire is on flat town streets, though pavements are uneven in places and kerbs can be high. The markets are crowded and can be tight for wheelchairs. Taxis are the practical option for the Mémorial ACTe and beaches. Contact the Mémorial ACTe (05 90 25 16 00) for access details.
rainyDay: Pointe-à-Pitre has good wet-weather options. Spend the morning at the Mémorial ACTe, then the Musée Saint-John Perse and the Musée Schoelcher, and the covered Marché Saint-Antoine. Skip the beach in heavy rain.
crowdTips: Guadeloupe had 284 cruise calls in 2024–25 and about 400,000 passengers, and Pointe-à-Pitre handles most of them. The terminal can berth three ships at once. Get to the markets early, before tour groups, and visit the Mémorial ACTe in the late morning or early afternoon.

faqs.q: Is Pointe-à-Pitre walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Place de la Victoire and the markets are a 10–15 minute walk on flat streets from Centre Saint-John Perse.
No. Ships dock at the Centre Saint-John Perse cruise terminal in the town centre.

faqs.q: How do I get from Pointe-à-Pitre cruise port to the Mémorial ACTe?
faqs.a: Walk to Place de la Victoire, then about 15 minutes south, or take a short taxi ride from the terminal stand.
Plage de la Datcha in Le Gosier is about 15 minutes by taxi. Sainte-Anne's beaches are 30–45 minutes by car.

faqs.q: What can I do in Pointe-à-Pitre in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The markets and Place de la Victoire in the morning, the Mémorial ACTe at midday, then a beach afternoon in Le Gosier.

faqs.q: Are shops open in Pointe-à-Pitre on Sunday?
faqs.a: Mostly no. Shops usually close on Sunday, and many close on Saturday and Wednesday afternoons and at lunchtime.

faqs.q: What currency is used in Guadeloupe?
faqs.a: The euro. Cards, especially Visa, are widely accepted; taxi drivers often take US dollars too.
Generally yes in daytime. Keep valuables secure in the markets and stick to busy streets on a quiet Sunday.
